data.title: Systemic sclerosis (scleroderma) — viva
data.summary: Connective tissue diseases · 12 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Systemic sclerosis (scleroderma)** (Connective tissue diseases)_

**Q1. Classify scleroderma (PYQ).**
- Localised scleroderma (morphoea) — skin ± underlying tissue, no internal organ disease: plaque, generalised, linear (including en coup de sabre and Parry–Romberg), deep, pansclerotic, mixed
- Systemic sclerosis (SSc): limited cutaneous (lcSSc — skin thickening distal to elbows/knees ± face; includes CREST), diffuse cutaneous (dcSSc — proximal limbs and trunk), SSc sine scleroderma (internal disease + antibodies without skin thickening), overlap syndromes
- Scleroderma-like disorders: scleredema, scleromyxoedema, nephrogenic systemic fibrosis, eosinophilic fasciitis, chronic GVHD, porphyria cutanea tarda, phenylketonuria, drug/toxin-induced (bleomycin, taxanes, vinyl chloride, silica, toxic oil, L-tryptophan)

**Q2. Explain the pathogenesis.**
- Triad: vasculopathy (endothelial injury → intimal proliferation, obliteration, Raynaud's, ischaemia) + immune activation (autoantibodies, T/B cells, IL-6, type I IFN) + fibrosis (TGF-β, PDGF, CTGF → myofibroblasts producing excess collagen in skin and organs)

**Q3. Describe skin features.**
- Raynaud's phenomenon (first symptom in >90%)
- Oedematous (puffy fingers) → indurated → atrophic phases
- Sclerodactyly (tapered, tight, shiny fingers with flexion contractures), digital pitting scars, ulcers on fingertips and knuckles, resorption of terminal phalanges (acro-osteolysis)
- Face: mask-like expressionless face, beaked nose, microstomia with radial perioral furrowing (purse-string mouth), loss of wrinkles
- Salt-and-pepper pigmentation (perifollicular retention with depigmentation), telangiectasias (matted), calcinosis cutis, nailfold capillary changes, pruritus (early)

**Q4. Write a short note on Raynaud's phenomenon (PYQ).**
- Episodic vasospasm of digital arteries on exposure to cold/stress — triphasic colour change: white (ischaemia/pallor) → blue (cyanosis) → red (reactive hyperaemia), with pain/numbness
- Primary (Raynaud's disease — young women, symmetrical, no ulcers, normal nailfold capillaries, ANA negative) vs secondary (SSc, SLE, MCTD, DM, Sjögren's, cryoglobulinaemia, vibration tools, thoracic outlet, drugs — β-blockers, ergots)
- Treatment: keep warm, gloves, stop smoking; calcium channel blockers (nifedipine SR, amlodipine) first line; losartan, fluoxetine, topical nitrates, PDE5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil), IV iloprost, bosentan (prevents new digital ulcers), botulinum toxin, sympathectomy

**Q5. Write a short note on CREST syndrome (PYQ).**
- Limited cutaneous SSc variant: Calcinosis cutis, Raynaud's phenomenon, oEsophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia (mat-like on face, hands)
- Anti-centromere antibodies (~50–90%); slower course; late complications — pulmonary arterial hypertension, primary biliary cholangitis

**Q6. Write a short note on calcinosis cutis (PYQ).**
- Deposition of insoluble calcium salts in skin
- Types: dystrophic (normal calcium/phosphate; damaged tissue — SSc, DM, lupus, tumours, trauma), metastatic (high Ca × P product — CKD, hyperparathyroidism, hypervitaminosis D, milk-alkali), idiopathic (scrotal calcinosis, subepidermal calcified nodule, tumoral calcinosis), iatrogenic (calcium gluconate extravasation, EEG paste), calciphylaxis (vascular calcification in CKD — painful necrosis, high mortality)
- Treatment: treat cause; diltiazem, bisphosphonates, warfarin (low dose), probenecid, colchicine (inflammation), sodium thiosulphate, excision, CO2 laser, lithotripsy

**Q7. What are the systemic features?**
- GI (90%): oesophageal dysmotility (dysphagia, reflux, Barrett's), watermelon stomach (GAVE), small bowel bacterial overgrowth, pseudo-obstruction, wide-mouthed colonic diverticula, faecal incontinence
- Lungs: interstitial lung disease (leading cause of death — dcSSc, anti-Scl-70), pulmonary arterial hypertension (lcSSc, anti-centromere)
- Kidney: scleroderma renal crisis — sudden hypertension, AKI, microangiopathic haemolysis (dcSSc, anti-RNA polymerase III, high-dose steroids >15 mg/day) — ACE inhibitors are life-saving
- Heart: myocardial fibrosis, arrhythmias, pericarditis
- Musculoskeletal: tendon friction rubs (dcSSc — poor prognosis), arthralgia, myopathy; also sicca, hypothyroidism, erectile dysfunction

**Q8. Antibodies and their associations.**
- Anti-topoisomerase I (Scl-70): dcSSc, ILD
- Anti-centromere: lcSSc/CREST, PAH, digital loss
- Anti-RNA polymerase III: rapid diffuse skin, renal crisis, cancer association (synchronous)
- Anti-U3 RNP (fibrillarin): PAH, myositis, young men of African descent
- Anti-PM/Scl: overlap with myositis; anti-Th/To: lcSSc with ILD/PAH

**Q9. Give the 2013 ACR/EULAR classification criteria.**
- Skin thickening of fingers of both hands extending proximal to MCP joints — sufficient alone (9 points)
- Otherwise add: skin thickening of fingers — puffy fingers 2 or sclerodactyly distal to MCP 4 (higher counted); fingertip lesions — digital ulcers 2 or pitting scars 3; telangiectasia 2; abnormal nailfold capillaries 2; PAH and/or ILD 2; Raynaud's 3; SSc-related antibodies (anti-centromere, Scl-70, RNA pol III) 3
- Total ≥9 = definite SSc (excludes scleroderma-like disorders)

**Q10. Investigations in SSc.**
- ANA (nucleolar/centromere/speckled), specific antibodies; nailfold capillaroscopy (giant capillaries, haemorrhages, avascular areas — 'scleroderma pattern': early, active, late)
- HRCT chest, PFT with DLCO, 6-minute walk, echocardiography ± right-heart catheterisation for PAH, NT-proBNP
- Renal function, BP, urine; upper GI endoscopy/manometry; skin score (modified Rodnan skin score, 17 sites 0–3, max 51)

**Q11. Management of SSc (organ-based).**
- Skin: methotrexate, mycophenolate (first choice for dcSSc skin + ILD), cyclophosphamide, rituximab, IVIG, autologous haematopoietic stem cell transplant for rapidly progressive dcSSc; physiotherapy
- Raynaud's/digital ulcers: as above (CCB, PDE5i, iloprost, bosentan)
- ILD: mycophenolate, cyclophosphamide, tocilizumab (anti-IL-6R), nintedanib (antifibrotic), rituximab, lung transplant
- PAH: endothelin receptor antagonists (bosentan, ambrisentan, macitentan), PDE5 inhibitors, prostacyclin analogues, riociguat
- Renal crisis: ACE inhibitor (captopril) titrated quickly, dialysis; avoid high-dose steroids
- GI: PPIs, prokinetics, rotating antibiotics for bacterial overgrowth
- Calcinosis and telangiectasia: as above; pulsed-dye laser for telangiectasia

**Q12. Prognosis.**
- 10-year survival ~70%; dcSSc worse; deaths mainly from ILD, PAH, cardiac disease; renal crisis mortality reduced by ACE inhibitors

## Quick spotter facts
- Sclerodactyly + microstomia + salt-and-pepper pigmentation — SSc
- Anti-Scl-70 → ILD; anti-centromere → CREST/PAH; anti-RNA pol III → renal crisis
- Renal crisis — ACE inhibitor

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Scleroderma); 2013 ACR/EULAR SSc classification criteria. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
